name: Per-person inter-organ coupling feature extraction (5-min aligned CGM-HR/activity)
purpose: Compute per-participant Pearson/Spearman/partial correlations between glucose and HR/activity on a common 5-min grid over the 10-day overlap, stratified by awake/sleep.
validation_notes: Used in legacy H-MIG01/H-MIG02 producing results/coupling_features.parquet, coupling_atlas.csv. Method description transcribed from legacy test_plan; not re-executed in this registry.

name: Kruskal-Wallis + Jonckheere-Terpstra trend with FDR correction and Cohen's d
purpose: Test monotonic differences of a per-person feature across 4 ordered diabetes-severity groups with FDR control and ordered-contrast effect size.
validation_notes: Primary statistical method in legacy H-MIG01 (FDR p=1.3e-19) and H-MIG02 (FDR p=1.04e-14). Transcribed from legacy test_plan.

name: Continuous wavelet transform coherence (Morlet omega0=6) with cone-of-influence exclusion
purpose: Decompose glucose-HR coupling into frequency bands (<30min..>8h) via wavelet coherence to test timescale-selectivity.
validation_notes: Legacy H-NEW01 executed a Welch-coherence variant (not full CWT) producing results/h_new01_frequency_coupling.csv; band directionality flip around 2h reported. Critic flagged >8h band and <30min negative control as unreliable.

name: Nested cross-validated classifier for coupling-vs-raw feature discrimination
purpose: Compare coupling-only vs raw-only vs combined feature sets for healthy-vs-insulin-dependent classification (AUROC) with nested CV.
validation_notes: Legacy H-MIG03: coupling-only AUROC=0.805, combined=0.952; coupling-only HbA1c R2=0.144 vs combined 0.674. Transcribed from legacy source.

name: Age/site-adjusted partial correlation with FDR for coupling-burden association
purpose: Estimate associations between coupling features and systemic burden markers (frailty index, allostatic load, homeostatic dysregulation) adjusting for age and site.
validation_notes: Legacy H-MIG04: primary partial r=0.148, FDR=2.18e-09 (glucose-HR vs frailty). Transcribed from legacy source.
